title: How EMEA law firms are moving to Intapp Compliance with Celeste
summary: Moving to Intapp Compliance with Celeste requires the right regional partner. How EMEA firms plan, execute, and expand their cloud compliance.
body_markdown:
Moving to Intapp Compliance with Celeste requires planning, the right execution approach, and a partner who understands regional complexity. Here’s what separates firms that complete the transition cleanly from those that stall.


### The case for moving now


EMEA law firms are moving compliance to the cloud. The cost of staying on-premises is clear: fragmented systems across geographies, manual intake that slows matter acceptance, compliance bottlenecks that eat into revenue the firm should be winning.


The firms pulling ahead have centralised their compliance data in the cloud. Once you do, Celeste starts working. Compliance teams apply judgment instead of processing forms. Intake moves faster. Matter decisions happen in hours, not days. The firm accepts work competitors still have pending.


This only works if compliance data is clean, centralised, and current. Legacy on-premises systems keep you stuck. Cloud-native compliance is the foundation for accepting more business without adding headcount.


Intapp Compliance with Celeste makes that possible. But migration requires planning, the right execution approach, and a partner who understands both the technical complexity and the firm dynamics that make compliance workflows matter.


### The migration questions every firm asks


When a managing partner or risk officer evaluates moving to Intapp Compliance with Celeste, a few questions come up consistently.


**Who does this work?** Compliance teams have limited bandwidth. Operations teams have competing priorities. Where does migration capacity come from?


**How long until we’re live?** Conflict checks, intake, and terms management can’t go dark. How do you migrate without disrupting the workflows that protect the firm?


**What changes for us?** Compliance teams know intake will be faster. More important: the firm can accept more business. Once your data is in the cloud, compliance stops consuming headcount and starts enabling growth.


These are regional questions too. EMEA firms operate across borders. Regulatory requirements shift country to country. Data residency matters. The solution that works for London doesn’t work for Madrid without adjustment.


The question firms rarely ask early enough: how much time do we have before implementation capacity is committed elsewhere.


### The capacity problem in EMEA


Implementation capacity is regional. Partners with deep EMEA expertise and legal sector credibility are not abundant. The best-positioned teams are booked. Firms that wait to finalize internal alignment often discover that the implementation partner they want is already committed to other projects months away.


The firms moving fastest in EMEA have done the work of partner engagement early. Sometimes months before they’ve fully decided to move. It sounds premature. It’s actually strategic. Starting the partner conversation before you’ve finalized the decision gives you clarity, flexibility, and better odds of hitting your timeline.


ROOX uses early engagement to bring risk, business, and IT teams together to identify what should be retained, simplified or redesigned across the firm’s compliance workflows and integrations. For firms operating across EMEA, this means distinguishing shared processes from local requirements and agreeing the decisions, dependencies and internal resources needed for a realistic migration plan.


### What a regional compliance migration actually looks like


Migration varies by firm. Some move all workflows at once. Others phase in: Intapp Conflicts first, then Intapp Intake, then Intapp Terms. For most EMEA firms, the phased approach works better because it keeps existing systems live while you modernise.


The firms that move successfully are the ones with a partner who understands regional complexity. ROOX has implemented Intapp solutions across EMEA markets: Spain, Portugal, the UK, France, Greece, Germany, and beyond. They understand how regulatory requirements differ country to country, not just how the software works.


They also understand that migration is a transition, not a project to finish and hand off.


ROOX plans each migration around the firm’s business priorities, helping teams continue to accept new clients and matters while adapting to change. The approach balances the pace of modernisation with the firm’s capacity to absorb it, keeping client service, effective risk management, and the needs of its people at the centre of the transition.


The right partner stays engaged post-launch. ROOX doesn’t disappear once you’re live. They help you optimise intake, build the business case for the next phase, and expand your cloud footprint.


Over 25 years of working alongside law firms, ROOX has built client relationships that span decades, developing a deep understanding of their businesses and playing an active role in their evolution. That enduring advisory role extends well beyond implementation: ROOX continues to help firms shape their processes and technology around changing business priorities, ensuring that each next step serves the people, clients, and ambitions of the firm.


### The payoff: compliance that scales without headcount


Most firms move to Intapp Compliance with Celeste to solve an immediate problem — a failing system, a compliance bottleneck, an operations team drowning in manual work.


The real payoff comes when compliance stops consuming capacity and starts enabling growth. Once your compliance data is centralised and in the cloud, Celeste works on your firm’s behalf. Intake moves faster. Conflicts clear faster. Decisions that took days happen in hours. Your compliance team applies judgment instead of processing forms. The firm says yes to work it would otherwise decline.


This shift depends on clean, centralised data. Legacy systems don’t provide that. Migrating to Intapp Compliance with Celeste with a partner like ROOX gets you there. You move from fragmented, on-premises workflows to a unified platform.


For EMEA firms, that means compliance scales with the firm, not against it.


### Start the conversation early


The firms completing Intapp Compliance with Celeste migrations cleanly in EMEA are the ones who started the partner conversation months before they expected to need one. Early engagement isn’t about pressure. It’s about clarity.


You’ll understand what a scoped migration actually looks like for your firm. You’ll know the timeline. You’ll have visibility into dependencies and decision points. And you won’t discover six months in that the implementation capacity you wanted is already booked.
